jp: スーパー{で|de-place}安[やす]い卵[たまご]{を/が|tai-ga-o}買[か]いたいです。
en: I want to buy cheap eggs at the supermarket.
why: The thing you want to do something with is marked by を or が with ～たい, not に, で or の.

jp: 来月[らいげつ]{は|wa-topic}旅行[りょこう]{が|ga-existence}ある{ので|node-because}、お金[かね]{が|tai-ga-o}もっと欲[ほ]しいです。
en: I have a trip next month, so I want more money.
why: The thing that is wanted is marked with が after 欲しい.

jp: この赤[あか]いセーター{を|tai-ga-o}着[き]てみたいです。
en: I want to try on this red sweater.
why: With ～てみたい the object takes を, because たい attaches to みる rather than directly to the verb.

jp: 私[わたし]{は|wa-topic}安[やす]いスマホ{が|tai-ga-o}欲[ほ]しいです。
why: The thing that is wanted is marked with が after 欲しい.

jp: 給料日[きゅうりょうび]{の|no-possessive}夜[よる]、友達[ともだち]{と|to-with}おいしい焼[や]き肉[にく]{を/が|tai-ga-o}食[た]べたいです。
en: On payday evening, I want to eat delicious grilled meat with my friends.
why: The food you want to eat is marked with を or が with ～たい.
